newsitem.title: UK: GLAXO FALLS 4 PCT, LATEST SECTOR VICTIM.
newsitem.headline: GLAXO FALLS 4 PCT, LATEST SECTOR VICTIM.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc fell to a two-month low on Wednesday as investors continued to take profits in the drug sector amid worries over patent expiries in the United States, market sources said.
By 1415 GMT, Glaxo shares were down 54p, or 4.24 percent, at 12.21 stg on volume of 7.7 million, one of the most active in the FTSE 100.
Other pharmaceutical shares also stumbled. Zeneca Group Plc stock lost 68-1/2p to 18.78 stg and Smithkline Beecham Plc fell 22-1/2p to 11.29 stg.

The UK drug sector outperformed the broader market by eight percent this year, to Friday. Since Monday, shares have followed their ADRs in New York lower as Morgan Stanely cut the U.S. sector to a "market weighting" from "overweight".
"I think the real reason (for the selloff) is that these stocks have performed very strongly and people are looking for an excuse to take some off the top," one analyst said.
"It's a profit-taking exercise and I don't think anything fundamental has changed," he said.
"On the fundamentals long term they are still on the buy side...I think sometime in the next month they will start to pick up again, particularly in Glaxo."
